title: Caddying at the country club and losing the job over a snake
summary: As a teenager Greer caddies for a brewery heiress, and is fired when he refuses to wade in after her ball because of a snake. He also notes the dull school-orchestra drummer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But me, when I was a kid, a teenager, I always liked to make money. I was out to make some kind of money. Well, a dollar was big money then, quarter, dime, I'd run errands for the grocery man. I would even run errands for the Chinaman in my town. I caddied when I was 14 years old, I caddied at a place, Deer Beach Country Club, which was very fashionable. This side of Asbury Park, New Jersey and I was caddying for some people at that time in Newark, New Jersey, biggest brewery in the east, one of the biggest was a brewery called Krueger, Krueger beer. They was very big, very wealthy people. I caddied for their youngest daughter. They grade caddies, you know, first class, second, I was her personal caddy.
So I was still going to school. I was going to

high school in Jersey, Long Branch. High School, still there, so every day we had a big school orchestra about 20 or 30 pieces, violins and everything, for assembly. We had assembly every morning, at class, and they would play them in and play them out and maybe sometime give a little concert so in the meantime, they had a drummer. The worst thing in the band was the drummer, but he was in a lot of my classes.

I had taken languages too and I was one of the good pupils-a German lady named Madam Bruskey, I was one of her good pupils in German. So anyway he was the dumbest guy, this guy, I said, 'how come you don't have to make up no classes.' He said, 'Oh, I got to rehearse,' and he'd get away with it.

So that went on a long time, so in the meantime I lost my job caddying by this incident. One day we was out and I was caddying for this girl. They didn't have them golf carts then were you could roll them -- you had to carry this heavy bag, and so we were on the course, and halfway to the first, to about the seventh or eighth hole in the rough, this -- she couldn't play no golf but she -- just a sport, because at that time when you see somebody on the golf course, they were very wealthy. So she hit the ball and it went into sort of a lake like. She said, 'hey, caddy, get that ball.' So all right, I slip out of my shoes and wade in and get this ball. Getting ready to step in the water, up come a snake

with the ball in his mouth. Now, I'm deathly scared of the snake, you know, so I look at the snake and I look at this broad. I said, no, she said 'what's the matter, get that -- ' she cursed a lot, 'get that so and so ball.' I say 'you want that so and so ball, you go get it.' She looked at me like I lost my mind. Here's this heiress to this fortune, youngest daugher. Plenty of money.

So she say, 'You're through'. So she gave me a little old dollar, got a dollar for walking around 18 holes and that was terrible. The bag weighed a ton, so I left the bag, --she anyway she want-- get it and walked off. So in the meantime, that went on -- I didn't have no job. I lost that job completely.
